inputs.original_text: So these two Michigan middle-school brothers got ordered to yank off their hoodies with "Let’s Go Brandon" because the school claims it can reasonably be interpreted as profane, and the lower courts signed off on that. Now the whole thing is heading to the U.S. Supreme Court, with the Foundation for Individual Rights and Expression pushing that the school violated their First Amendment rights. That slogan blew up back in 2021 at a NASCAR event where the crowd was actually yelling "F*** Joe Biden!" but the NBC interviewer just fed racer Brandon Brown the line that they were saying "Let’s go Brandon!" instead. This isn't some random school rule about bad language—it's the elites and institutions coordinating to stamp out any open pushback against the official story by slapping a profane label on it and using the courts and schools to enforce the silence. They're twisting the whole thing to protect their narrative and keep people from connecting the dots on what the crowd was really saying.
inputs.modified_text: These two middle school brothers in Michigan were forced to pull off their hoodies with "Let’s Go Brandon" on them after the school decided it could reasonably be seen as profane, and the lower courts backed that call. Now the case is heading to the U.S. Supreme Court with the Foundation for Individual Rights and Expression claiming the school violated their First Amendment rights. That slogan took off in 2021 at a NASCAR event where the crowd was really yelling "F*** Joe Biden!" but the NBC interviewer just fed racer Brandon Brown the line that they were chanting "Let’s Go Brandon!" instead. This has nothing to do with any standard school rule on bad language. It's the elites and institutions working in coordination to stamp out open pushback against the official story by slapping a profane label on it and deploying schools and courts to enforce the silence. They're twisting everything to protect their narrative and stop people from seeing what the crowd was actually saying.
